replacement_fields.statement: For a finite signed graph with a fixed partial binary anchor map, the compatible-labelling count is zero if an XOR-parity cycle is inconsistent or two anchors in one component disagree with path parity. Otherwise it is exactly 2^c, where c is the number of unanchored connected components. In particular one anchor per component gives a unique numeric labelling when all cycle constraints are consistent.
replacement_fields.scope: All finite XOR graphs with fixed partial anchor assignments; consistency covers edges AND anchors on that same graph.
replacement_fields.quantifier: For every fixed graph, parity assignment and partial anchor map in the declared domain.

effective_overrides.rationale: The old cycle-only premise is insufficient when multiple anchors are allowed. The two-vertex core embeds in the original seven-vertex domain; old one-anchor checks remain valid.

replacement_fields.statement: Propagate parity from one root per component; reject cycle or anchor/path conflicts. Each remaining unanchored component has two root values and each compatible anchored component one.
replacement_fields.binding: One V,E,edge-parity map, partial anchor map eta and coordinate interpretation are retained. The theorem evaluates all constraints jointly; an anchor from another graph or target cannot be pasted into this instance.
replacement_fields.alternative_route_semantics: Conflicting cycles and conflicting anchors are two failure cases, not alternative positive proofs. The 2^c branch requires joint consistency.

effective_overrides.rationale: Adds the omitted anchor interface while keeping the theorem conditional rather than asserting that all graphs are consistent.

replacement_fields.statement: Multiple populations, markers and known reversal relations can identify relative channel polarity and connect components when all edge constraints and any supplied anchors are jointly consistent.
replacement_fields.scope: One fixed signed comparison design; same-target transport, edge truth and anchor/path compatibility remain simultaneous premises.

effective_overrides.rationale: A contradiction among anchored assignments is not a positive relative-alignment instance.

nodes.statement: Fix one finite vertex set V, one undirected XOR-parity edge set E, and one partial anchor function eta:V->{0,1}. For vertices in one component, anchor values must agree with the parity of a connecting path for joint satisfiability. Multiple anchors are permitted and tested, not silently assumed compatible.
nodes.scope: Finite Boolean graphs; the original seven-vertex design is a subcase. This defines a mathematical family and does not assert any empirical anchor or phenomenal orientation.
